name: The Greenwood
summary: The last great forest of Aurelith: old, deliberate, and not fond of strangers. Under the Root-Wardens of the Greenwood Compact it is less a territory than a signatory — the oldest treaty in the world was sworn here, and greenfolk say the trees were witness.

geography.character: old-growth broadleaf and grey pine, dense canopy, way-paths that move with the seasons

notable_sites.name: The Eldertree
notable_sites.note: The greenfolk's unique deity is said to be this tree, or to live in it, or to dream it — theology varies by grove.

notable_sites.name: The Moot-Lawns
notable_sites.note: Clearings kept open for Compact councils; fire is forbidden within sight of them.

lore_notes: Veyra's vow — the Greenwood Compact of the Age of Stone — binds the greenfolk to answer any realm that asks under the old forms; none have asked in four centuries.
Wood-cutters licensed by the Wardens take deadfall only. The few who took living wood are names spoken to frighten children on both sides of the forest edge.
adventure_hooks: A Northmarch mining charter's survey stakes appear inside the treeline; somebody moved them, and nobody admits which side.
Greenfolk envoys ask outsiders to carry a sealed acorn to the Septuary — fast, and without opening the box.
